title: Wk. 9 of vibecoding an MMO
author: Electrical-Pig
selftext:
I was previously doing a two-section posting system about (1) user-retention and (2) what I'm learning, but frankly user-retention is simply a lost cause unless I spend some $$ on ads, which I can't afford. So instead, we're just having fun with an overpriced dead-end hobby! Let's get into it.

So if you haven't seen my previous posts, I've been vibe coding this bad boy since opus 4.7. 

The big bummer bummer part is that Opus 5.5 has improved so much that I could probably start over in just a few hours. Instead, this has taken hundreds of hours, constant tweaking, and maxing out my top-tier subscription every single week, ***and*** building myself other helper-tools like a sprite/tile editor (see [Myrling](https://josiah-turnquist.github.io/myrling-sprite-editor/)).

Which by the way, not very useful now that Opus 5.5 can generate pretty good pixel art. (although all models, including whatever Pixellab uses, struggle to make good 16x16 art, so it's still not perfect).

The most noteworthy comment about this iteration is that Opus 5.5 came out and revolutionized everything. And really made me question if this is all a waste of time and I should switch careers from coding -> blue collar. It's that good, and it will only get better.

**Exhibit A - causing my 27 year-midlife crisis.**

For kicks and giggles I had Opus **one-shot** a *significantly* *more exciting 3D version of my game*. It's a massive world, with amazing physics and basically all the content that I hand-curated in my 2D MMO.

3D Link: [3d.eldermyr.com](http://3d.eldermyr.com/) (not multiplayer)

2D MMO Link: [www.eldermyr.com/](http://www.eldermyr.com/) (multiplayer)

  
What do we say, boys? Do we go back to trades? (I'm a technical project manager)

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: I like when people are trying and not making one shot slops. As somebody who is on Week 9 of making a game with AI myself - respect 🫡

replies.author: Electrical-Pig
replies.body: Oh hey you're the fishing guy! I saw yours posts on X btw, I hope that was actually you and somebody isn't stealing your content?

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: No I don't use X, it was somebody else showing my game, I had to check it out on X because people were telling me the same thing :D

replies.author: Electrical-Pig
replies.body: He has a lot of followers and is claiming to be you. Could be a different guy tbh. Good work gets a lot of attention.

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: I saw one guy posting constantly, didn't see him claiming to be me, but a bit sad he never put a post toward my reddit posts or mention me. But it's still some sort of exposure I guess.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body:
So I played a bit 3D version. I really love it, vibe and the game feel is just right I feel like. I will play some more probably, it's just that I'm working on my game in the background and my Macbook is gonna melt if I keep doing both. I wish there was a way to see level of the minion either that I attack or something. When I click on it it obviously just uses an attack. Small lvl number in a circle around minion would be nice (maybe there is a way to toogle it but I wasn't going too much into it). 

I also think there is no benefit (at least what I played so far) in picking first person view, as you have to aim up and down while 3rd person camera allows me to just shoot at the npc without focusing on up and down target. That is a huge benefit for picking 3rd person view. Just few notes for now.

replies.author: Electrical-Pig
replies.body:
Great feedback! The 3D version was built on the 2D version, where a lot of these things would've been the mage hugely overpowered and imbalanced. 

However, one I have time to continue the 3D version, this will all be very helpful in steering the direction of it. Thanks for the review pass!

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body:
Okie so 2D version is the one to test :D 

Maybe honestly drop 3D version entirely (If you envisioned your game as 2D) it might be way too hard to focus on 2 things at once, but your choice.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body: I guarantee you that if you don’t know what to require from AI to build an MMO, it will never be one, because even the simplest stuff for an MMO needs to be designed entirely differently different and takes 2-10x times the effort and code of the single-player version.
